new_statements.translation: g) Pitch. Tumak is a language that makes use of pitch. It has level tones and rising and falling contour tones. [...] h) Phonological remarks. We prefer to indicate here only a few phonological problems raised by the phonetic inventory set out above, and to refrain from proposing a phonology of Tumak. [...] Tones — Three level tones are attested, high, mid and low (minimal triplets bá/bā/bà, híg/hīg/hìg, lág/lāg/làg). The following contour tones are attested: ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given anywhere in the accessible description: Tumak is described as a tone language with three contrastive level tones (H, M, L) plus contour tones on single (short) vowels; stress/accent is simply not mentioned, and the author explicitly declines to offer a full phonology. Google full-text search indicates that Caprile's dedicated 1977 phonology chapter (pp. 79-86) likewise describes 'trois registres... trois tons ponctuels' and contains no accent/stress vocabulary.
new_statements.exceptions: none (no stress statement); tonal remarks: haut-moyen contour not attested; doubled vowels in the transcription mark contour tones, not length (p. 19 fn. 1)
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical citation forms in a phonetic inventory; syllable canon V/CV/VC/CVC, words up to three syllables. Statement concerns tone only; silence on stress is an absence, not a claim that stress does not exist.
new_statements.identity_note: All of Caprile's data are from the Tumak of Goundi (tumak proper, Moyen-Chari), autonym [baŋ tumagaan]; the Motun/Mod and Mawer varieties sometimes grouped under iso tmc are not covered. Glottocode tuma1260 applies directly.

sources.note: Nothing. Sections: formes canoniques, types syllabiques (V, CV, VC, CVC; no clusters), vowels, consonants and their distributions, then g) 'la hauteur mélodique' (p. 25: Tumak 'utilise la hauteur mélodique', level and contour tones) and h) remarques phonologiques (p. 26: 'Trois tons ponctuels sont attestés, haut, moyen, et bas' plus a list of contour tones pp. 26-27; author explicitly abstains from proposing a full phonology). The words accent / accentué / intensité do not occur in the excerpt (pages read as images, not only scanned).
